paras.text: This is a player vs player (PvP) mission pack for head-to-head gameplay using Killzone: Tomb World or Killzone: Gallowdark. While players battle one another, they must also contend with NPOs (non-player operatives) — 3rd party adversaries that will attack either player and disrupt the battle. The players will have to adapt their game plan to manage the threats NPOs pose.

This mission pack is designed to be used alongside other mission packs that use three objective markers, such as Preliminary Ops (Kill Team Core Book) or Approved Ops (available separately). It can still be used with other mission packs (e.g. Multiplayer Ops) if you adjust the rules to accommodate it.

This mission pack also provides rules for Tomb World event cards. Use as much as you feel is appropriate – if you think all the extra rules would be too much, feel free to ignore certain parts of this mission pack, or ignore certain parts of the mission pack you’re using it with (e.g. tac ops and selecting a primary op in Approved Ops).

In Tomb World Maps, you’ll find three maps to use with this mission pack (ignore maps 4–6). You can roll one D3 to randomly determine a map, or select the one that interests you most. Alternatively, you can use PvP maps designed for Killzone: Tomb World or Killzone: Gallowdark, such as those found in Approved Ops (available separately).
Excluding rooms within drop zones, the first time each room is opened, or the first time a player operative is within it (whichever comes first), determine the NPOs within that room as follows:
1. Roll one D3 to determine how many.
2. Roll 2D6 for each NPO to determine what type it is using the table in NPO Datacards section.
3. Starting with the player that opened the room, each player alternates setting up an NPO within that room until they’ve all been set up.
4. Each NPO should be set up ready with a Conceal order, more than 2" from other operatives (if possible).

NPOs don’t gain any CP. In each Strategy phase after the first, NPOs have the two STRATEGIC GAMBITS detailed below. NPOs are first in the alternating order, and NPOs will always pass after both of their required STRATEGIC GAMBITS have been used.
For the first NPO STRATEGIC GAMBIT, shuffle all used Tomb World event cards back into the deck, then randomly draw a new one.

For the second NPO STRATEGIC GAMBIT, the player who didn’t win the initiative roll-off sets up one NPO reinforcement. That player rolls 2D6 to determine the type of NPO using the table. They then set that NPO up ready with a Conceal order so that a randomly determined hatchway’s access point is within its control range (there are six hatchways, so assign each a number and roll one D6 – it doesn’t matter if the hatchway is closed).

For the purposes of incapacitating enemy operatives for VPs (e.g. the kill op, tac ops, etc.), ignore NPOs. This means you cannot score VPs for incapacitating them, but also your opponent cannot score VPs when an NPO incapacitates one of your operatives. Note this means that friendly operatives incapacitated by NPOs are not counted towards your opponent’s kill grade.

Once NPOs have been discovered and set up, they will activate. After the final player activates, but before the first player activates again, one ready NPO will activate. In other words, they activate last in the alternating sequence. If there are multiple ready NPOs, the players roll-off and the winner decides which will activate. When it activates, use its behaviour and the threat principle (explained opposite). NPOs cannot counteract. The turning point ends once all the players’ operatives and the NPOs are expended.

Each NPO’s datacard has a behaviour that determines what they do. Each behaviour will specify what order they have when activated. Whenever an NPO would perform an action, perform the first action it can do from its behaviour. If it cannot do any, it’s expended.

The threat principle is used when making decisions for activated NPOs (who to charge, fight, shoot etc.). However, it differs in this mission pack from the Joint Ops mission pack, as there will rarely be an option that’s equally worse for both players. Instead, whenever an NPO activates, the closest player operative it could fight/shoot/move towards (as determined by the NPO’s behaviour) is the NPO’s target. If multiple players’ operatives are equally as close, roll-off and the winner decides. The opponent of the player who controls the NPO’s target will control the NPO for that activation, and they must make every effort to fight/shoot/move the NPO so that it threatens its target (as determined by its behaviour).

An operative cannot perform this action during the first turning point, while within control range of an enemy operative, or if that objective marker has already been looted during this turning point.

Friendly operatives will control that objective marker at the end of this turning point.

If friendly operatives control an objective marker that is swept, you score 1 VP

At the end of the third and fourth turning point, you can remove Dominate tokens from friendly operatives that are in the killzone and aren’t incapacitated. For each you remove, you score 1VP.
You cannot score more than 3VP from this op per turning point.

sections.title: Joint Ops: Deadly Sniper Mission Pack

paras.text: This is a player vs environment (PvE) mission pack for cooperative or solo gameplay using Killzone: Volkus. It involves a player or players battling together against a collection of NPOs (non-player operatives) stubbornly defending a stronghold with a deadly sniper on the top level. If playing cooperatively, you are still one ‘player’. This means you don’t double your CP, equipment selections, etc.; you must manage them between you.

If you wish, one player can be the game master. They will manage the NPOs – move them, roll dice for them, etc. – whilst one or more other players control a kill team. The game master will still control the NPOs as the rules in this mission pack specify, they just take this pressure and decision-making away from the player(s) so they can focus on their own operatives and having fun!

Here you will find three missions. They are intended to be played in sequence – win or lose – to tell the narrative of an ongoing battle against an expert sniper. The missions include specific maps designed using Killzone: Volkus, all showing the same area but with different angles of approach. You will have to think carefully about how to position your operatives, as many sections of the map are exposed to the sniper. What’s more, due to their positioning and the Silent weapon rule, the sniper will likely be untargetable during the first two missions, so you may have to win those missions without engaging them.

The player(s) use one kill team. If you are playing solo, simply select your kill team as normal. If you are playing cooperatively, either select a kill team as normal and split the operatives between you, or take half of any kill team each. If it’s an odd number, round up (or down for more of a challenge). If you’ve taken separate teams, remember that some rules specify certain operatives through keywords, so one kill team’s rules won’t necessarily interact with another’s.

Your kill team will fight against procedurally generated non-player operatives (known as NPOs). Unlike your highly trained operatives, NPOs are mostly standard soldiers from their army – frontline troops, guards, etc. – but they are backed up by a deadly sniper. As such, you don’t select a kill team for them. Instead, you use the appropriate datacards from NPO Datacards section. Alternatively, you can create your own datacards to accurately reflect their stats using existing kill teams as a guide – just ignore rules that wouldn’t be appropriate.

Each mission specifies how many NPOs you should include to accompany the sniper, determined by their combined Wounds stat. To increase or decrease the difficulty, simply increase or decrease this number as appropriate.
Don’t select equipment for NPOs in this mission pack.
When rolling off to decide who has initiative, roll one dice for the NPOs and one dice for the solo/co-op kill team. If the NPOs win the roll-off, they will always choose to have initiative.

When making decisions for NPOs, use the threat principle: go with the option that’s worst for you. This can determine which ready NPO activates, how an NPO moves, shoots and fights, how to resolve their dice, etc. There are a few examples below (containing decisions in order of priority) that you can use as a guide, but if one option feels worse for you – in particular to stop you winning the mission – go with that. If you still cannot decide, randomly choose one.

An assault upon an enemy stronghold has faltered and one of your senior officers has been wounded and pinned down by sniper fire. You have been chosen to lead an extraction mission. Brave the sharpshooter’s fire, repel the enemy and ensure that the injured officer is returned to safety

NPOs: One SNIPER NPO set up on the highest Vantage terrain of Stronghold B. Then, any combination of NPOs with a combined Wounds stat of up to 90. They are set up with a Conceal order wholly within Stronghold B, either not visible from the player drop zone or in cover.

Rescue: Friendly operatives can perform the Pick Up Marker action on the objective marker. Whenever a friendly operative is carrying the objective marker, worsen the Hit stat of its weapons by 1 and it cannot be removed and set up again (e.g. it cannot FLY).
Escape: Player operatives can move wholly over their killzone edge. Any that do so have escaped – remove them from the killzone.

Set them up with a Conceal order on the killzone floor within Stronghold B and wholly within 6" of the NPO killzone edge.

In the Ready step of each Strategy phase, if any NPOs are within 2" of the objective marker, the battle might end: at the end of that turning point, if any NPOs are within 2" of the objective marker and no friendly operatives are within 6" of it, the battle ends and the player(s) lose.

The battle also ends if the player(s) have no operatives left in the killzone. In this instance, if a player operative carrying the objective marker has escaped, the player(s) win. Otherwise, the player(s) lose.

They are set up with a Conceal order wholly within the NPO drop zone; spread them out as evenly as possible between areas 1-4 on the mission map, either not visible from the player drop zone or in cover.

Reserve: When setting up each friendly operative before the battle, you can set it up in reserve instead: place it to one side instead of in the killzone. Each friendly operative that was incapacitated during the previous mission must be set up in reserve. In the first Firefight phase, each friendly operative set up in reserve is activated as normal. When it is, set it up in the killzone in a location it can be placed wholly within a distance equal to its Move stat from the left half of your killzone edge. The operative is treated as performing the Reposition action (spend the AP accordingly), then continue its activation as normal.

Escape: Player operatives can move wholly over the left half of the NPO or player killzone edge. Any that do so have escaped – remove them from the killzone. Note that the edge an operative escaped from determines its set up location in mission 3.

The battle ends when the player(s) have none of their operatives left in the killzone. If more than 50% of their operatives have escaped over the NPO killzone edge, the player(s) win. Otherwise, they lose.

You have the sniper surrounded, but they remain a lethal threat. The enemy are trapped within their last remaining strongpoint. Your operatives must fight their way through the defenders and put an end to the target.

NPOs: One SNIPER NPO set up on the highest Vantage terrain of Stronghold B. Then, any combination of NPOs with a combined Wounds stat of up to 90. They are set up with a Conceal order wholly within Stronghold B, either not visible from the player drop zone or in cover.

Flanking Forces: When setting up player operatives before the battle, each that escaped over the NPO killzone edge in mission 2 must be set up in the player drop zone on the right side of the mission map. All other player operatives must be set up in the player drop zone on the left side of the mission map.

Defend the Stronghold: When setting up equipment before the battle, add a barricade to the centre of Stronghold B. For the purposes of the threat principle and making decisions for NPOs, they should do what best defends Stronghold B. For example, they should only leave the stronghold if it realistically threatens player operatives and reduces the player(s)’ chances of winning the mission.

No Escape: Whenever a player operative wholly within Stronghold B is shooting an NPO that’s also wholly within Stronghold B, the player operative’s ranged weapons have the Seek Light weapon rule. Note this means they can target the SNIPER.

Reinforcements: In each Strategy phase after the second, if half the NPOs are incapacitated (ignore the SNIPER when determining this), they call in reinforcements as a STRATEGIC GAMBIT. Randomly select two incapacitated NPOs (excluding Heavy NPOs) or one incapacitated Heavy NPO. Set them up wholly within 4" of the centre of an NPO killzone edge (randomise each edge for each operative).

At the end of any turning point after the third, the player(s) can choose to end the battle. The battle also ends if all player operatives are incapacitated. When the battle ends, if player operatives control the stronghold terrain feature, they win. Otherwise, they lose. Player operatives control the stronghold terrain feature if the total APL of player operatives wholly within it and on the killzone floor is greater than that of NPOs.

The Great Gun Fires Mission Pack
The Great Gun Fires Mission Pack | Expansion | 3 | 1.0 | October 2024

Volkus’ capital hive city, Hive Fissilicus, is dominated by the Massif Ballistus, known also as the Great Gun. This colossal ordnance rises from the city’s heart, a mechanical behemoth from Humanity’s distant past. Whenever it is fired, the fumes and recoil released lay waste to those areas beneath its atmosphere-scraping barrels.

This mission is designed to be played using the game sequence and the Transmission crit op from the Kill Team Core Book. In this mission, your kill teams must extract crucial intelligence scattered during a previous battle, but the irreversible hymnals of firing have already begun to echo throughout the city. Your kill teams must seize their objectives and exfiltrate before the gun’s destructive recoil reduces your area of operations to a wasteland of corpse-strewn rubble.
Facing the Firing: In the Set up the Battle step, randomly determine one neutral killzone edge to also be the Massif Ballistus killzone edge.
The Great Gun: A different mission rule is applied during each turning point, as specified below:

The operation of the Great Gun is laced in mysticism and ritual. These arts are maintained through each holy Day of Firing. When such a day dawns, the populace of Volkus are led in song by the priesthood of the Adeptus Ministorum, the voices of billions heralding the impending firing of the Great Gun. The shrines of the Massif Ballistus echo with chanting and prayers that build to a fever pitch as the firing approaches. In these last moments, operatives rush to complete their mission with heightened urgency and motivation.

The chanting halts and prayers fall silent. The eyes of the faithful turn upwards to the sky-scraping barrel in awestruck anticipation…

As the Great Gun’s twin barrels erupt, a storm of searing gases are unleashed upon the city below. Ash and fire explode across the battlefield, searing exposed flesh and stunning everyone in the vicinity.

In the Ready step of the Strategy phase, inflict D3+1 damage on each operative that doesn’t have intervening Heavy terrain within its control range between it and the Massif Ballistus killzone edge (roll separately for each).

Then, each operative that doesn’t have intervening Light or Heavy terrain within its control range between it and the Massif Ballistus killzone edge gains one Shockwave token. Friendly operatives with a Shockwave token cannot be activated or perform actions until each friendly operative without a Shockwave token is expended. Whenever an operative with a Shockwave token is expended, remove that token.

The ground shakes violently beneath the operatives’ feet as the Great Gun’s subterranean mechanisms absorb the terrifying recoil of the Massif Ballistus. Even the most agile of warriors are driven to the soil by the force of these quakes.

Each NEMESIS operative needs two blank datacards to record its rules. Download and print the blank datacards below, then begin creating your NEMESIS operative by completing the following steps.

Select one of the following allegiance keywords and add it to the operative’s datacard: AELDARI, CHAOS, IMPERIUM, LEAGUES OF VOTANN, NECRON, ORK, T’AU EMPIRE, TYRANID. Other operatives that don’t share that keyword cannot be used in the same kill team as it. Each NEMESIS operative has an allegiance trait determined by its allegiance keyword (see step 5).

Select the NEMESIS operative’s size: this determines many of its starting stats and how many weapons it can have. The bigger the operative’s size, the more powerful it is, so less operatives will be used alongside it (as explained in the Joint Ops and Nemesis Ops mission packs). In the examples section, we have specified the size of some suitable Citadel miniatures, but if your miniature isn’t present or you are customising one, simply use the size that feels most appropriate.

The bigger the operative’s size, the bigger its base usually is. Unless the killzone map is designed for them, larger bases (in particular 100mm or more) can be awkward as there may be locations where the operative cannot be placed. Therefore, use your discretion when selecting the operative’s size and/or setting up the killzone for your battles. For example, close quarters killzones (e.g. Killzone: Tomb World) aren’t recommended for large NEMESIS operatives.

*Control is a new stat for NEMESIS operatives that’s used for the APL stat in all instances except spending action points. For example, use it for determining control of markers, and for rules that compare a dice result to the operative’s APL stat.

NEMESIS operatives can activate twice per turning point, but activation restrictions and action point limits vary depending on if it’s an NPO or player operative. This is detailed in the mission pack you are playing.

If the operative is a player operative, you can choose its order and actions (other than those mentioned at the end of this section, it cannot perform mission actions or unique actions from equipment). However, if it’s an NPO (non-player operative), you must select its behaviour, which specifies its order and actions during the battle. In the examples section, we have specified the behaviour of some suitable Citadel miniatures, but again you’re free to use the one that feels most appropriate.

This NPO will move towards the enemy to fight them, but will seek cover on its way. When activated, if it’s a NEMESIS NPO or will perform the Fight or Charge action during that activation, give it an Engage order. Otherwise, give it a Conceal order.
Charge the closest player operative via the shortest possible route.
Reposition towards the closest player operative, to cover if possible (a subsequent Dash action can fulfil this).
Dash towards the closest player operative, to cover if possible.

This NPO will move to an ideal position to shoot the enemy. When activated, if it’s a NEMESIS NPO or will perform the Shoot action during that activation, give it an Engage order. Otherwise, give it a Conceal order.
Fall Back. If possible, to a location where there’s a valid target that isn’t obscured, if not, to a location that’s appropriate for the NPOs to better win the mission.

Reposition. If possible, to a location where there’s a valid target that isn’t obscured, if not, to a location that’s appropriate for the NPOs to better win the mission (a subsequent Dash action can fulfil these).
Dash. If possible, to a location where there’s a valid target that isn’t obscured, if not, to a location that’s appropriate for the NPOs to better win the mission.

Charge the closest player operative via the shortest possible route.
Reposition towards the closest player operative, to cover if possible (a subsequent Dash action can fulfil this).
Dash towards the closest player operative, to cover if possible.

NEMESIS operatives can perform the Operate Hatch and Breach mission actions, and NEMESIS NPOs will do so where necessary to fulfil their behaviour. However, close quarters killzones (e.g. Killzone: Tomb World) aren’t recommended for large NEMESIS operatives.

Select a number of weapons for the operative up to the quantity permitted by its size. Weapons with the Selection x weapon rule count as x selections instead (e.g. a weapon with Selection 2 counts as two of your permitted selections). Any selections you don’t use grant you an extra nemesis trait selection in the Traits step. We have provided a list of common weapons and their potential alternatives in this section, but if a weapon you have in mind isn’t present, simply use the one that feels most appropriate – even if they belonged to different allegiances, many weapons would share common stats and rules.

You cannot select weapons that aren’t representative of weapons the operative has (e.g. if a model has a meltagun it cannot be a heavy bolter), and if it’s been modelled with more weapons than the quantity permitted, ignore the less significant ones. The operative cannot use weapons that aren’t selected for its datacard (e.g. it cannot use grenades from universal equipment).

Alongside weapons, traits differentiate your NEMESIS operative from others. First, your NEMESIS operative has one allegiance trait determined by its selected allegiance keyword. These rules can be found on the relevant allegiance card:
LEAGUES OF VOTANN: Acquisition at All Costs
TYRANID: Will of the Hive Mind

You then select one nemesis trait for your NEMESIS operative (see table below). This is best selected to capture the narrative of the operative (making it more aggressive, tough, accurate, etc.). Each weapon selection you didn’t use in the Weapons step grants you an extra nemesis trait selection, but you cannot select a nemesis trait the operative already has.

Note that these rules are written from the perspective of the NEMESIS operative being friendly. If it’s being created as an enemy operative (e.g. an NPO), the rule should be used from the perspective of the NPOs, as determined by the threat principle.
Whenever this operative is shooting against or fighting against a ready enemy operative, if two or more fails are rolled for it, one of them can be discarded to re-roll another.
Whenever this operative is wholly within enemy territory, its weapons have the Balanced weapon rule.

Whenever an operative is shooting this operative, if this operative is wholly within your territory, one of its defence dice can be retained as a normal success without rolling it (in addition to a cover save, if any).

Whenever this operative is shooting against or fighting against an enemy operative that contests an objective marker, or and area of the killzone that determines victor (e.g. flanks), this operative’s weapons have the Balanced weapon rule.

Whenever this operative is within 3" of another friendly T’AU EMPIRE operative, this operative’s ranged weapons have the Accurate 1 weapon rule.
Ignore changes to this operative’s stats from being injured (including its weapons’ stats).
Whenever an operative is shooting this operative with a weapon that has a Normal Dmg stat of 3 or less, improve this operative’s Save stat by 1.
Whenever this operative performs the Charge action during its activation, its melee weapons have the Severe and Shock weapon rules until the end of that activation.
Whenever this operative is fighting or retaliating, you can resolve one of its successes before the normal order. If you do, that success must be used to block.
Whenever this operative is shooting during its activation, if it hasn’t performed any other actions during that activation, its ranged weapons have the Punishing weapon rule.

Whenever this operative is shooting the closest valid target within 8" of it, its ranged weapons have the Lethal 5+ weapon rule; if the weapon already has that weapon rule, it also has the Severe weapon rule.

This operative’s melee weapons have the Ceaseless weapon rule; if the weapon already has that weapon rule, it has the Relentless weapon rule. Worsen the Hit stat of this operative’s ranged weapons by 1.
Ignore any changes to this operative’s weapon stats from being injured.
When this operative finishes moving during the Charge action, inflict D3+3 damage on one enemy operative within its control range.
Once per battle, when an attack dice inflicts damage on this operative, you can ignore that inflicted damage.
Whenever an operative is shooting this operative from more than 8" away, attack dice cannot be re-rolled.
Ignore any changes to this operative’s Move stat from being injured.
Whenever an attack dice inflicts damage of 4 or more on this operative, roll one D6: on a 5+, subtract 1 from that inflicted damage.

If this operative is incapacitated, before it’s removed from the killzone, inflict D6+1 damage on each other operative within 3" of it (excluding operatives with Heavy terrain wholly intervening between them and this operative).

Finally, choose a name for your operative, which is the name of the miniature it is or represents. You can also designate it a suitable moniker, tag or call sign, to evoke its background or (in)famous deeds.

NEMESIS operatives are very different to normal operatives, therefore they have some important core rules to reflect this that can be found in this section. Note that when a NEMESIS is a player operative, it doesn’t gain a faction keyword. For example, it cannot be selected for your kill team’s faction rules that specify an operative with that faction keyword.

This operative cannot be placed on Vantage terrain higher than 2" from the killzone floor.
Whenever this operative would perform the Fight action, the distance requirements of its control range can be changed to 1" horizontally and 4" vertically until the end of that action.
This operative can move through other operatives (excluding NEMESIS operatives).
Ignore all changes to this operative’s APL and if it’s a player operative, APL changes don’t affect the 5AP you can spend per turning point.
In the Firefight phase, whenever you determine this operative’s order, you cannot select Conceal.
This operative cannot be in cover or obscured by Light terrain, terrain parts less than 3" tall or terrain that’s not wholly intervening.

Whenever another operative is performing the Shoot action, being within control range of other operatives doesn’t prevent this operative from being selected as a valid target. In other words, this operative can be shot while within control range of friendly operatives.
This operative can move through terrain parts less than 2" tall. It cannot move through Accessible terrain (excluding hatchways) unless that terrain is also less than 2" tall.

Whenever this operative would finish a move in a terrain feature less than 2" tall, temporarily remove that terrain feature from the killzone, then return it when this operative leaves that location; if it’s an equipment terrain feature, remove it from the battle instead.

This section contains four new mission packs that feature nemesis operatives for head-to-head, cooperative and solo games of Warhammer 40,000: Kill Team. This includes rules and missions for two infamous nemesis operatives: the Ambull and the Archivist.
This is a new way to play Kill Team that involves your operatives fighting with and/or against a formidable nemesis, from mighty war machines to hulking monsters.
First you must decide on your mission pack, determined by the type of game you want to play:
Joint Ops is for solo/cooperative games with and/or against a NEMESIS operative.
Nemesis Ops is for head-to-head games where both players use a NEMESIS operative.

The Ambull and the Archivist mission packs are specifically designed for those NEMESIS operatives. Both mission packs contain a Joint Ops and Adversary Ops mission. Adversary ops is for head-to-head games, but the NEMESIS operatives are a third party that can attack either player.

With some house rules, you can use NEMESIS operatives in other mission packs (e.g. Approved Ops). NEMESIS operatives may need to be restricted from certain mission rules, so read through the mission first and do whatever feels right.

Each mission pack has a game sequence detailing how to set up and play the battle. The Joint Ops and Nemesis Ops mission packs each have an optional campaign to link your games together - the outcome of each game affects which mission you play next.

When selecting operatives before the battle, you must also decide on the NEMESIS operative(s) to be used. The Nemesis Custom Builder section explains in detail how to create your own NEMESIS operative, in which you customise the operative’s rules as appropriate to fit a miniature of your choice. The Nemesis Operative Examples section gives some examples of pre-created NEMESIS operatives you can use instead of creating your own, or as a guide.

This is a player vs environment (PvE) mission pack for cooperative or solo gameplay using Killzone: Volkus. It involves a player or players battling together against a collection of NPOs (non-player operatives) with one or both sides using a NEMESIS operative. If playing cooperatively, you are still one ‘player’. This means you don’t double your CP, equipment selections, etc.; you must manage them between you.

If you wish, one player can be the game master. They’ll manage the NPOs - move them, roll dice for them, etc. - while one or more other players control a kill team. The game master will still control the NPOs as the rules in this mission pack specify, they just take the pressure and decision-making away from the player(s) so they can focus on their own operatives and having fun!

The Joint Ops Missions section contains four missions. For a one-off game, you can randomly determine a mission, or select the one that interests you most. Alternatively, you can link the games together in a campaign. Begin with mission 01: Erosion of Power, then all subsequent missions are determined by the outcome of the previous one, as shown in the Campaign Progress Chart below. This diagram is just to give you an overview of the possible outcomes, so you don’t need to learn it all now - each mission will explain what to do next.

The player(s) select one kill team. If the player(s) are using a NEMESIS operative, create it using the Nemesis Custom Builder, being mindful of its allegiance keyword and size; it must have the same allegiance keyword as your selected kill team (e.g. IMPERIUM, CHAOS, etc.). When selecting operatives, if the player(s) are using a NEMESIS operative, select a reduced number to accompany that operative as shown in the table below. The row you use is determined by the kill team’s normal starting number of operatives (i.e. excluding the NEMESIS operative), and the column you use is your NEMESIS operative’s size. If operatives count as a different number of selections (e.g. BROOD BROTHER MAGUS counting as two, or two PSYCHIC FAMILIAR operatives still counting as one), this also applies to this table.

For example, when using a small NEMESIS operative, if the rest of the kill team is usually 10 operatives, 7 other operatives could be taken alongside that NEMESIS operative. These 7 must still fulfil the normal operative requirements for that team (e.g. weapon and operative limits), but the player(s) can select which three aren’t included (e.g. they could leave out a LEADER operative that’s usually required). Once you’ve selected your kill team and its operatives, if you are playing cooperatively, split the operatives between you.
KILL TEAM’S NORMAL NUMBER OF OPERATIVES

Your kill team will fight against procedurally operated non-player operatives (known as NPOs). All NPOs, including a NEMESIS NPO if relevant, must have the same allegiance keyword. If the NPOs are using a NEMESIS operative, create it using the Nemesis Custom Builder, being mindful of its allegiance keyword and size. The other NPOs your kill team will fight against are more standard soldiers. As such, you don’t select a kill team or equipment for them. Instead, use the appropriate datacards for miniatures in your collection, found in the Nemesis Operatives card pack.

Each NPO (excluding NEMESIS) has a Points stat on their datacard that’s used to determine how many NPOs are set up at the start of the battle. This amount depends on the NEMESIS NPO in the battle (if any), as specified in the Nemesis NPO Size table of each mission. For example, in mission 1, if the NPOs have a medium NEMESIS NPO, up to 8 points of NPOs must be set up before the battle.

Any unused points are saved in the NPO Reinforcements pool. NPO STRATEGIC GAMBITS and NPO activation cards (see below) will also add points to the NPO Reinforcements pool, then require you to set up NPOs using those points (remove points from the pool for operatives set up).

When rolling off to decide who has initiative, roll one dice for the NPOs and one dice for the player(s). If the NPOs win the roll-off, they’ll always choose to have initiative. NPOs don’t gain any CP, but do use STRATEGIC GAMBITS (as specified by the mission). NPOs will always pass after all their required STRATEGIC GAMBITS have been used.

Each NPO’s datacard has a behaviour that determines what they do, detailed on behaviour cards and repeated in Behaviour (NPO Only). Each behaviour will specify what order they have when activated. Whenever an NPO would perform an action, perform the first action it can do from its behaviour. If it cannot do any, it’s expended.

This mission pack uses a deck of cards numbered 1-13 to determine NPO activation. Whenever it’s the NPOs’ turn to activate, draw a card from the deck and consult the NPO Activation Cards table on each mission to determine how to resolve it. Once you’ve resolved it, discard that card. If you draw a card but cannot activate the operative the table specifies, skip that NPO activation and alternate back to the player(s).

NPOs cannot counteract in this mission pack, but whenever it’s the NPOs’ turn to activate, still draw a card from the deck (even if all NPOs are expended). This is because the activation card may have other rules effects, such as setting up reinforcements.

The NPO activation deck remains secret and cards are only revealed when drawn. However, player(s) can inspect the discard pile at any time to inform them of activation cards that remain in the deck. In the Ready step of each Strategy phase, and whenever you would draw a card from the deck but it’s empty, shuffle all NPO activation cards (including discarded ones) together to recreate the deck.

A deck of NPO activation cards are provided with this publication, but if you don’t have them, you can use those provided in Kill Team: Terror on Devlan, or substitute them with standard playing cards. Simply take all the cards from one suit and treat the following cards as numbers: Ace is 1, Jack is 11, Queen is 12 and King is 13.

NEMESIS NPOs can be activated twice per turning point as a result of the NPO activation cards. Player(s) activate their friendly NEMESIS operative (if any) twice per turning point, but they cannot activate it a second time until all other friendly operatives are expended. Nemesis player operatives cannot move more than 12" per turning point and the player(s) cannot spend more than 5AP for it in total per turning point.

When making decisions for NPOs, use the threat principle: go with the option that’s worst for you. This can determine which ready NPO activates (if there are multiple options from the activation card), how an NPO moves, shoots and fights, how to resolve their dice, etc. There are a few examples below (containing decisions in order of priority) that you can use as a guide, but if one option feels worse for you - in particular to stop you winning the mission - go with that. If you still cannot decide, randomly choose one.
An NPO activation card requires a non-NEMESIS NPO to be activated, but multiple are ready, so the player(s) activate the NPO that:

Can perform the Shoot or Fight action (as determined by its behaviour), and is the most threatening to do so (e.g. is more likely to incapacitate a player operative, is more likely to prevent the player(s) winning, etc.).
Is not in cover from a player operative.
Is closer to a player operative.
NPOs must be set up as specified by the mission, but if there are multiple valid options, the player(s) set up each NPO so that it’s:
More likely to prevent the player(s) winning.
Better able to perform the Charge, Shoot or Fight action (as determined by the higher priority of the NPO’s behaviour).
Evenly spaced throughout the specified area and more than 2" from other operatives.
An NPO performs the Fight action and multiple player operatives are within its control range. It fights the player operative that:
An NPO performs the Shoot action and multiple player operatives are valid targets. It shoots the player operative that:
If you want to increase or decrease the difficulty of the missions, here are a few methods:
Change the number of NPOs being set up. Start with one more (or less) points worth of NPOs, and whenever you add points to the NPO Reinforcements pool, add one more (or less).

If you find a particular type of NPO more (or less) challenging, use a different type instead. For example, if NPOs have the IMPERIUM keyword and INTERCESSOR NPOs are proving difficult, use BATTLE SISTER and CADIAN SHOCK TROOPER NPOs instead.
When drawing NPO activation cards, draw two and select the result that’s worse for you (or better).
Select a kill team as described in Joint Ops Kill Team Selection.
Determine the mission as described in Joint Ops Missions.

Set up the killzone and objective markers as specified by the mission map. The mission maps use Killzone: Volkus, but you can use a different killzone and set up terrain features similarly to what’s specified. Drop zones are assigned to the player(s) and NPOs as specified by the mission map.

Create a NEMESIS operative for each side that’s using one, following the Nemesis Custom Builder. Remember, the allegiance keyword selected must be the same for all operatives on that side (e.g. IMPERIUM, CHAOS, etc.). The player(s) select their operatives for the battle, adhering to the selection requirements in their kill team’s rules. Note that if they’re using a NEMESIS operative, its size limits the number they can select.

The player(s) select which NPO datacards they’ll be using. Remember, all NPOs must have the same allegiance keyword, matching the NEMESIS operative’s if they’re using one. The player(s) select up to four equipment options (four in total, not four per player). Each option cannot be selected more than once. Don’t select equipment for NPOs.
The player(s) gain 2CP (two in total, not two per player). NPOs don’t gain any CP.
The player(s) set up all their equipment that’s set up before the battle (ladders, etc.).
The mission will specify how many points of NPOs to set up, and where. If any are set up before the battle, set them up now with a Conceal order.
The player(s) then set up their operatives. Each operative must be set up wholly within their drop zone and must be given a Conceal order.
If a NEMESIS operative is too large to be set up wholly within its drop zone, set it up with its base touching its killzone edge instead.
In the first turning point, the player(s) have initiative.
The battle ends when the mission specifies.

The mission’s victory condition will specify how to determine whether it’s a win or a loss (major or minor if relevant) for the player(s). This then determines the next mission, as explained in the mission’s campaign progress chart.

Mission commanders have demanded a daring strike against the enemy’s supplies, with the intention of choking off their capacity to coordinate reinforcements. The target nexus sites, however - whether of communications, energy or materiel - are sure to be guarded by the foe’s most potent assets.

NPOs: Set up the NEMESIS NPO (if any) wholly within the NPO drop zone, then set up the remaining NPOs using the table below wholly within NPO territory. As an NPO STRATEGIC GAMBIT in each turning point after the first, add D3 points to the NPO Reinforcements pool, then set up NPO reinforcements from that pool. Each reinforcement must be set up ready with a Conceal order with its base touching the NPO killzone edge.
Player operatives (excluding NEMESIS) can perform the following mission action:

One objective marker the active operative controls is sabotaged until the end of the turning point. If this is the third time this action has been performed during this turning point, you gain 1 Sabotage point. Whenever an NPO activation card is drawn, you can spend 1 of your Sabotage points to discard that card without resolving its effects and skip that NPO activation.

An operative cannot perform this action during the first turning point, while within control range of an enemy operative, or if that objective marker has already been sabotaged during this turning point.

Add 1 point to the NPO Reinforcements pool. If you have enough points in the pool, set up any reinforcements. Each reinforcement must be set up ready with a Conceal order with its base touching the NPO killzone edge.
Activate one NEMESIS NPO. During that activation it has an APL of 3. It cannot activate more than twice per turning point, and it cannot move more than 12" per turning point.

The result is determined by the total VP scored during the battle.

A pocket of the enemy is massing and full-scale encirclement cannot be deployed in time. Your operatives are called upon to strike in a bold, multipronged assault to utterly disrupt the foe’s escape route and seize ground for further offensives.

NPOs: Set up the NEMESIS NPO (if any) wholly within the NPO drop zone, then set up the remaining NPOs using the table below wholly within NPO territory. As an NPO STRATEGIC GAMBIT in each turning point after the first, add D3 points to the NPO Reinforcements pool, then set up NPO reinforcements from that pool. Each reinforcement must be set up ready with a Conceal order with its base touching the NPO killzone edge.

Reserve: When the player(s) are setting up their operatives before the battle, half must be set up as normal. The remaining half must be set up outflanking: place them to one side instead of in the killzone. Whenever an outflanking operative is activated during the first turning point, immediately expend it.

Outflank: As a STRATEGIC GAMBIT in the second turning point, the player(s) select a neutral killzone edge to also be the outflank edge. Remove the objective marker nearest to that killzone edge that’s within player territory from the killzone. Then, whenever an outflanking operative is activated, set that operative up with an order of your choice wholly within player territory with its base touching the outflank edge (it’s no longer outflanking). Then, continue its activation as normal.

If player operatives control 1 or more objective markers, remove 1 point from the NPO Reinforcements pool (if any). If player operatives don’t control any objective markers, add 1 point to the NPO Reinforcements pool (note that you don’t set up any reinforcements yet). In either case, after you have done so, activate one non-NEMESIS NPO.

Add 1 point to the NPO Reinforcements pool. If you have enough points in the pool, set up any reinforcements. Each reinforcement must be set up ready with a Conceal order with its base touching the NPO killzone edge.
Activate one NEMESIS NPO. During that activation it has an APL of 3. It cannot activate more than twice per turning point, and it cannot move more than 12" per turning point.

At the end of any turning point after the third, the player(s) can choose to end the battle.
The result is determined by the number of objective markers contested/controlled by player operatives at the end of the battle.
Player operatives control two objective markers and contest the third.
Player operatives control two objective markers and don’t contest the third.
Player operatives control one or less objective markers.

In the wake of their primary mission, your operatives’ planned extraction is compromised as vengeful enemy forces converge on their position. A signals array provides the nearest location from which the kill team’s allies can be contacted to coordinate a new exit strategy, but the circling foe know this too.

NPOs: Set up the NEMESIS NPO (if any) with its base touching the NPO killzone edge, then set up the remaining NPOs using the table below wholly within NPO territory. As an NPO STRATEGIC GAMBIT in each turning point after the first, add 1 point to the NPO Reinforcements pool, or D3 points if a player operative has performed the Coordinate Extraction mission action (see below), then set up NPO reinforcements from that pool. Each reinforcement must be set up ready with a Conceal order with its base touching the NPO killzone edge.
Ambush Advantage: Whenever an NPO is shooting or fighting during the same turning point in which it was set up, its weapons have the Accurate 1 weapon rule.
Player operatives (excluding NEMESIS) can perform the following mission action:
Randomly determine one killzone edge (excluding the players’) to be the escape edge.

An operative cannot perform this action during the first turning point, while within control range of an enemy operative, if it doesn’t control the objective marker, or if this action has already been performed during the battle.

Escape: Once the escape edge has been determined, player operatives can move over that edge while wholly within NPO territory; if any part of their base does, they’re removed from the killzone and have escaped.

Add 1 point to the NPO Reinforcements pool, or 2 points if a player operative has performed the Coordinate Extraction mission action. If you have enough points in the pool, set up any reinforcements. Each reinforcement must be set up ready with a Conceal order with its base touching the NPO killzone edge.
Activate one NEMESIS NPO. During that activation it has an APL of 2. It cannot activate more than twice per turning point, and it cannot move more than 12" per turning point.
Activate one NEMESIS NPO. During that activation it has an APL of 3. It cannot activate more than twice per turning point, and it cannot move more than 12" per turning point.

The result is determined by the number of player operatives that have escaped at the end of the battle.
Three quarters or more of the player operatives escaped.
Half or more of the player operatives escaped.

A fortified position is under threat. The aggressors have deployed two powerful weapons that can bring the defences down, but they must be ushered into the ideal position and protected as they are conveyed on these routes. The strongpoint’s defenders, however, will not allow them to do so unopposed.

NPOs: Set up the NEMESIS NPO (if any) wholly within their assigned drop zone, then set up the remaining NPOs using the table below as specified by the Offence/Defence rule. As an NPO STRATEGIC GAMBIT in each turning point after the first, add D3 points to the NPO Reinforcements pool, then set up NPO reinforcements from that pool. Each reinforcement must be set up ready with a Conceal order wholly within the Offence drop zone if the NPOs have the role of Offence, or wholly within the Base area and with the Defence killzone edge within its control range if the NPOs have the role of Defence.

Offence/Defence: The player(s) take the role of Offence or Defence. This is determined by the previous mission, unless it’s a one-off game, in which case they choose or randomise. NPOs take the other role. When setting up Defence operatives before the battle, they must be set up wholly within the Defence drop zone. When setting up Offence operatives before the battle, any can be set up in reserve: place them to one side instead of in the killzone. In the Firefight phase, Offence operatives set up in reserve are activated as normal. Whenever one is activated, set it up with an order of your choice wholly within the Offence drop zone (it’s no longer in reserve). Then, continue its activation as normal.

Safeguard Munition Routes: There are two objective markers and they each start at a location marked 1 on the mission map. At the end of each turning point, if the Offence controls an objective marker, they can move that marker to the next location (i.e. from 1 to 2 or 2 to 3). If the Defence controls an objective marker, they can move that objective marker to the previous location (i.e. from 3 to 2 or 2 to 1).

Threat Principle: Whenever an NPO is performing an action in which it moves, contesting an objective marker that NPOs don’t control is a high priority (if possible) for the purposes of the threat principle.

Add 1 point to the NPO Reinforcements pool. If you have enough points in the pool, set up any reinforcements. Each reinforcement must be set up ready with a Conceal order as described in the NPOs mission rule, depending on which role the NPOs have.
Activate one NEMESIS NPO. During that activation it has an APL of 2. It cannot activate more than twice per turning point, and it cannot move more than 12" per turning point.

Activate one NEMESIS NPO. During that activation it has an APL of 3. It cannot activate more than twice per turning point, and it cannot move more than 12" per turning point. If that NPO has already activated twice this turning point, add 1 point to the NPO Reinforcements pool.

This is a player vs player (PvP) mission pack for head-to-head gameplay, where both players are using a NEMESIS operative. Players pit these mighty adversaries against one another alongside the supporting operatives from their kill teams. This mission pack also has a strategic element, allowing you to influence the mission for each game.

The Nemesis Ops Missions section contains four missions. Before the first game, each player puts a Strategy card face down, or puts a number of dice in their hand that corresponds to their selected strategy’s number. They then reveal their selections simultaneously. The mission is determined by the strategies selected, as shown in the chart below. The missions and their maps use the terms Advancing player, Holding player and Manoeuvring player, relating to the players who chose those strategies.
If the Advance (1) and Hold (2) strategies were selected, play mission 04: Fracture Defences.
If the Hold (2) and Manoeuvre (3) strategies were selected, play mission 02: Flanking Strike.
If the Manoeuvre (3) and Advance (1) strategies were selected, play mission 03: Counterassault.
If the same strategies were selected, play mission 01: Territorial Gains.

You can link the games together in a campaign. If you do, for each subsequent game, repeat the above process for determining the mission. If a player lost the previous game, they must select and reveal their strategy first. The winner of the previous game can then use this information to select their strategy, however, they cannot select a strategy that would repeat the previous mission. The winner of the campaign is the first player to win three games.

Each player selects one kill team. Each player must also create a NEMESIS operative using the Nemesis Custom Builder; be mindful of its size, and it must have the same allegiance keyword as your kill team (e.g. IMPERIUM, CHAOS, etc.). When selecting operatives for their kill team, each player must select a reduced number to accompany their NEMESIS operative, as shown in the table below. The row each player uses is determined by their kill team’s normal starting number of operatives (i.e. excluding the NEMESIS operative), and the column they use is their NEMESIS operative’s size. If operatives count as a different number of selections (e.g. BROOD BROTHER MAGUS counting as two, or two PSYCHIC FAMILIAR operatives still counting as one), this also applies to this table.

For example, when using a small NEMESIS operative, if the rest of the kill team is usually 10 operatives, 7 other operatives could be taken alongside that NEMESIS operative. These 7 must still fulfil the normal operative requirements for that team (e.g. weapon and operative limits), but the player can select which three aren’t included (e.g. they could leave out a LEADER operative that’s usually required).
KILL TEAM’S NORMAL NUMBER OF OPERATIVES

Each player must activate their friendly NEMESIS operative twice per turning point, but they cannot activate it a second time until all other friendly operatives are expended. It cannot move more than 12" per turning point and each player cannot spend more than 5AP for it in total per turning point.

Each player selects a kill team for the battle. Determine the mission by selecting strategies. Remember, if a player lost the previous game they select and reveal their strategy first, but the previous mission cannot be repeated when the winner selects theirs. If playing missions 1-3, roll-off - the winner decides who has initiative. In mission 04: Fracture Defences, the Advancing player has initiative. Assign drop zones to players as specified by the mission map. Set up the killzone and objective markers (if any) as specified by the mission map. The mission maps use Killzone: Volkus, but you can use a different killzone and set up terrain similarly to what’s specified. Some missions have alternate ways of setting up terrain features and objective markers (see mission rules).

Each player creates a NEMESIS operative using the Nemesis Custom Builder. Remember, the allegiance keyword selected must be the same as in the player’s selected kill team (e.g. IMPERIUM, CHAOS, etc.). Each player secretly selects their remaining operatives for the battle, adhering to the selection requirements in their kill team’s rules and in Nemesis Ops Kill Team Selection. Note that their NEMESIS operative’s size limits the number they can select. They then reveal their selections simultaneously. Each player secretly selects up to four equipment options. Each option cannot be selected more than once per player. They then reveal their selections simultaneously. Each player gains 2CP.

Each player alternates setting up an item of equipment that’s set up before the battle (ladders, etc.), starting with the player with initiative. Note it’s item by item, not option by option. Starting with the player with initiative, each player sets up their NEMESIS operative, then each player alternates setting up one half of their remaining operatives (rounding up). When a player sets up an operative, it must be set up wholly within their drop zone and must be given a Conceal order. If a NEMESIS operative is too large to be set up wholly within its drop zone, set it up with its base touching its killzone edge instead.
In the first turning point, the players roll-off and the winner decides who has initiative. If it’s a tie, the player who didn’t have initiative during set up decides.

The battle ends after four turning points have been completed. Note that mission 4 has a mission rule that can result in the battle ending later than this. If one player has no operatives in the killzone but the battle hasn’t ended, the other player plays out each remaining turning point until it does. The player with the most VP is the winner. If both players are tied, it’s a draw.

Ahead of advancing forces, operatives have been tasked with securing the route for an anticipated spearhead. These fringes of the foe’s territory are a dangerous frontier, where an elite enemy kill team prowls, but seizing this channel of attack can swing the battle’s momentum in moments.

Terrain Features: Don’t set up terrain features as normal (the mission map set up is an example only). Instead, pair up terrain features according to similar size, ideally with the same Heavy or Light terrain type (e.g. using Killzone: Volkus you could pair 2 strongholds, 2 large ruins, 2 heavy rubble etc.). If there’s an odd number of terrain features, discard the additional one instead. Starting with the player with initiative, each player alternates selecting a terrain feature from each pair to add to their terrain pool (the opponent adds the other from the terrain pair to their own pool). Once each player has completed their terrain pool, starting with the player with initiative, each player alternates setting up terrain features from their pool one at a time. Whenever a player sets up a terrain feature, it must be wholly within their territory, and more than 2" from the killzone edges and other terrain features.

Objective Markers: Don’t set up objective markers as normal (the mission map set up is an example only). After terrain features have been set up, the player without initiative sets up one objective marker on the centreline, equally between each player’s territory and more than 6" from the killzone edges. Then, starting with the player with initiative, each player sets up one objective marker wholly within their territory and more than 3" from their drop zone, the killzone edges and other objective markers. Each objective marker must be set up on the killzone floor.
Friendly operatives (excluding NEMESIS) can perform the following mission action:
One objective marker the active operative controls is secured by your kill team until your opponent’s kill team secures that objective marker.
An operative cannot perform this action during the first turning point, or while within control range of an enemy operative.
At the end of each turning point after the first, you score 1VP for each objective marker secured by your kill team.
At the end of the battle, if the enemy NEMESIS operative is incapacitated, you score 2VP; if it’s injured but not incapacitated, you score 1VP.

Entrenched in defensive positions, one force surveys the enemy operatives advancing from cover to cover. What at first appears to bear the hallmarks of a suicidal strike escalates rapidly, with the attackers’ reinforcements surging from the flanks to bypass the defenders’ firing lines.

Reserve: When the Manoeuvring player is setting up their operatives before the battle, half must be set up as normal. The remaining half must be set up outflanking: place them to one side instead of in the killzone. Whenever an outflanking operative is activated:

If it’s the first turning point, expend it. If it’s the second turning point, set it up with an order of your choice wholly within Manoeuvring player territory with its base touching a neutral killzone edge (it’s no longer outflanking). Then, continue its activation as normal.

Flanks: Holding player territory is divided into two flanks (left and right) as shown on the mission map. Friendly operatives contest a flank while wholly within it. Friendly operatives control a flank if the total APL stat of those contesting it is higher than that of enemy operatives. Remember to use the Control stat for NEMESIS operatives rather than APL, and note it’s only related to Holding player territory - an operative isn’t contesting a flank while within Manoeuvring player territory.
At the end of the third and fourth turning point:
For each flank friendly operatives control, you score 2VP.
For each flank friendly operatives contest but don’t control, you score 1VP.
At the end of the battle, if the enemy NEMESIS operative is incapacitated, you score 2VP; if it’s injured but not incapacitated, you score 1VP.

An aggressive push into enemy territory by an elite group of operatives and their looming ally is on the brink of puncturing the foe’s lines, but a counterassault has been prepared to tear the throat from the incursion. As the invaders push forwards, their hunters close in for the kill.

Objective Markers: Don’t set up objective markers as normal (the mission map set up is an example only). After terrain features have been set up, each player sets up one objective marker, starting with the Advancing player. Each objective marker must be set up on the killzone floor, on the centre of the objective line (see mission map), and more than 3" from the killzone edges and the opponent’s territory.

Reserve: When the Manoeuvring player is setting up their operatives before the battle, they cannot set up any in the killzone. They can set up any in reserve instead: place them to one side instead of in the killzone. Whenever an operative set up in reserve is activated, set it up with an order of your choice wholly within Manoeuvring player territory with its base touching a killzone edge, or the Manoeuvring player killzone edge if it’s a NEMESIS operative (it’s no longer in reserve). Then, continue its activation as normal.

Table Quarters: The killzone is quartered by the centreline and the objective line (see mission map). Friendly operatives contest a killzone quarter while wholly within it. Friendly operatives control a killzone quarter if the total APL stat of those contesting it is higher than that of enemy operatives. Remember to use the Control stat for NEMESIS operatives rather than APL.
Friendly operatives (excluding NEMESIS) can perform the following mission action:
One objective marker the active operative controls is secured by your kill team until your opponent’s kill team secures that objective marker.
An operative cannot perform this action during the first turning point, or while within control range of an enemy operative.
At the end of the third and fourth turning point:
For each objective marker secured by your kill team, you score 2VP. For each killzone quarter wholly within your opponent’s territory that friendly operatives control, you score 1VP.
At the end of the battle, if the enemy NEMESIS operative is incapacitated, you score 2VP; if it's injured but not incapacitated, you score 1VP.

An enemy defensive point must be breached to break a stalemate in a grinding war of attrition. A kill team are tasked with escorting a powerful ally capable of ravaging the site, alert at all times to the foe’s own specialists who are rumoured to be hidden throughout this area.

Defensive Terrain: The Advancing player has initiative before the battle. When setting up the killzone, the Holding player can change the set up of terrain features wholly within their territory from what’s specified on the mission map. Each that they change must be set up again wholly within their territory and more than 2" from other terrain features.

Objective Markers: Don’t set up objective markers as normal (the mission map set up is an example only). After terrain features have been set up, the Holding player sets up three objective markers. One must be wholly within their drop zone, while the other two must be wholly within their territory and more than 2" from their drop zone. Each objective marker must be set up on the killzone floor, more than 2" from the killzone edges and more than 4" from each other.

Reserve: When the Advancing player is setting up their operatives before the battle, they can set up any in reserve instead: place them to one side instead of in the killzone. Whenever an operative set up in reserve is activated, choose one of the following:

Set it up with an order of your choice wholly within Advancing player territory with its base touching a killzone edge (it’s no longer in reserve); the operative is treated as performing the Dash action (spend the AP accordingly), then continue its activation as normal. Alternatively, expend it. Operatives in reserve at the end of the battle are incapacitated.

Besieged: In the Initiative step of each Strategy phase, the Advancing player can re-roll their initiative roll. At the end of each turning point after the third, if the Advancing player has friendly operatives within Holding player territory, they can roll one D6: on a 3+, the game continues for another turning point.
The Advancing player’s operatives (excluding NEMESIS) can perform the following mission action:
Roll a number of D6 equal to the number of action points you spend on this action. If any result is a 3+, remove one objective marker the active operative controls from the killzone.
An operative cannot perform this action during the first turning point, or while within control range of an enemy operative.
At the end of the battle, for each objective marker in the killzone, the Holding player scores 2VP. For each that isn’t, the Advancing player scores 2VP.
At the end of the battle, if the enemy NEMESIS operative is incapacitated, you score 2VP; if it’s injured but not incapacitated, you score 1VP.

This mission pack contains rules for the Ambull nemesis operative and its two Borewyrm Infestations, alongside two missions designed specifically for them. The first mission is player vs environment (PvE) for co-operative or solo gameplay against NPO adversaries, including the Ambull and Borewyrm Infestations. The second mission is player vs player (PvP), but the players must also contend with the Ambull and Borewyrm Infestations as third party adversaries, attacking either player and disrupting the battle. The Ambull nemesis operative can be used in other missions at your discretion.

The AMBULL and BOREWYRM INFESTATION operatives are NPOs, meaning you use the threat principle and behaviour rules for them as normal. The AMBULL NPO is also a NEMESIS operative; it has the Extra Defence and Bulky core NEMESIS rules, but it doesn’t have Towering Size. The AMBULL and the BOREWYRM INFESTATION NPOs both have the following additional rules:

In the Set Up Operatives step, the AMBULL and BOREWYRM INFESTATION NPOs are always set up in reserve: place them to one side instead of in the killzone (they cannot be activated while in reserve). They are set up in the killzone as determined by cards drawn from the Intruder deck (see Intruder Deck).

The AMBULL and BOREWYRM INFESTATION NPOs use a deck of cards to determine their activations, but it only consists of NPO activation cards 1-8. Whenever it’s the Ambull NPO side’s turn to activate, if an AMBULL or BOREWYRM INFESTATION NPO is in the killzone, draw a card from the deck and consult the table below to determine how to resolve it. Once you’ve resolved it, discard that card. The AMBULL NPO can be activated twice per turning point, and BOREWYRM INFESTATION NPOs can be activated multiple times per turning point. If you draw a card but none of it can be resolved, simply skip that NPO activation. For example, if you draw an NPO activation card and you are instructed to activate a BOREWYRM INFESTATION NPO, but there’s only an AMBULL NPO in the killzone, discard that card and then the player(s)/next player activates.

The NPO activation deck remains secret and cards are only revealed when drawn. However, players can inspect the discard pile at any time to inform them of activation cards that remain in the deck. In the Ready step of each Strategy phase, and whenever a card would be drawn from the deck but it’s empty, shuffle all NPO activation cards (including discarded ones) together to recreate the deck.
Activate one ready BOREWYRM INFESTATION NPO, or an expended one if none are ready.

Roll one D6 separately for each operative (excluding AMBULL and BOREWYRM INFESTATION NPOs) on the killzone floor. If the result is less than the operative’s Save stat, inflict damage on it equal to the dice result halved (rounding up).
Inflict D6 damage on each operative (excluding AMBULL and BOREWYRM INFESTATION NPOs) within 6" of the AMBULL NPO (roll separately for each).
Activate the AMBULL NPO. During that activation it has an APL of 2. It cannot activate more than twice per turning point, and it cannot move more than 12" per turning point.

Activate the AMBULL NPO. During that activation it has an APL of 3 and can perform two Fight actions. It cannot activate more than twice per turning point, and it cannot move more than 12" per turning point.

Draw without replacement. Use New turning point in the Ready step; an empty deck reshuffles before the next draw. Progress is saved for this tab.

The remaining NPO activation cards (9-13) are used to create a separate Intruder deck. At the end of each turning point after the first, and whenever an operative finishes performing a mission action (excluding Operate Hatch), draw a card from the Intruder deck (unless it’s empty) and consult the table below to determine how to resolve it, then remove it from the game.

Set up one BOREWYRM INFESTATION NPO ready with a Conceal order (it’s no longer in reserve). If this card was drawn due to a mission action, set that NPO up within control range of the active operative; if this card was drawn due to the end of the turning point, set it up with a random objective marker within its control range, and if possible within control range of enemy operatives (randomise if necessary).

Set up the AMBULL NPO ready with a Conceal order (it’s no longer in reserve). If this card was drawn due to a mission action, set that NPO up within control range of the active operative; if this card was drawn due to the end of the turning point, set it up with a random objective marker within its control range, and if possible within control range of enemy operatives (randomise if necessary).
Cards are removed from the battle when drawn. This deck does not reshuffle; reset only for a new battle. Progress is saved for this tab.

Determine the mission between 1: The Hidden Enemy (Joint Ops) or 2: Decaying Generatorium (Adversary Ops). If playing mission 1, select a kill team for the player(s) as described in Joint Ops Kill Team Selection. If playing mission 2, each player selects their own kill team. If playing mission 2, roll-off - the winner decides who has initiative. Set up the killzone and objective markers as specified by the mission map. Both mission maps use Killzone: Volkus, but you can use a different killzone and set up terrain features similarly to what’s specified. Drop zones are assigned to the player(s) and NPOs as specified by the mission map. If playing mission 2, the player with initiative selects one drop zone, and their opponent has the other.

The player(s) select their operatives for the battle, adhering to the selection requirements in their kill team’s rules. If playing mission 2, each player does this secretly before revealing their options simultaneously. If playing mission 1, the player(s) select which NPO datacards they’ll be using for the sentries NPOs. If playing mission 1, the player(s) select up to four equipment options (four in total, not four per player). If playing mission 2, each player secretly selects up to four equipment options before revealing them simultaneously. Each option cannot be selected more than once per player(s)/player. Don’t select equipment for NPOs. If playing mission 1, the player(s) gain 2CP (two in total, not two per player). If playing mission 2, each player gains 2CP. NPOs don’t gain any CP.

The player(s) set up all their equipment that’s set up before the battle (ladders, etc.). If playing mission 2, each player alternates setting up an item of equipment, starting with the player with initiative (note it’s item by item, not option by option).

The mission will specify how many NPOs are set up and where. In both missions, the AMBULL and BOREWYRM INFESTATION NPOs are set up in reserve. If playing mission 1, Sentry NPOs are set up before the battle, so set them up now with a Conceal order. The player(s) then set up their operatives. Each operative must be set up wholly within their drop zone and must be given a Conceal order. If playing mission 2, each player alternates setting up one third of their kill team (rounding up), starting with the player with initiative.

If playing mission 1, roll-off in the first turning point for the player(s) and both sides of NPOs to establish a player order. If playing mission 2, the players roll-off in the first turning point and the winner decides who has initiative. If it’s a tie, the player who didn’t have initiative during set up decides.

The battle ends when the mission specifies. In mission 2, if one player has no operatives in the killzone but the battle hasn’t ended, the other player plays out each remaining turning point until it does. In both missions, the mission’s victory conditions will specify how to determine the winner.
