Core Nemesis Rules: Extra Defence, Bulky.
Rad-Maggot Symbiosis: Whenever this NPO is activated, it regains a number of lost wounds equal to its APL+1. Its APL is determined by the NPO activation card.
Small: Whenever this NPO has a Conceal order and is in cover, it cannot be selected as a valid target, taking precedence over all other rules (e.g. Seek, Vantage terrain) except being within 2".

After infiltrating an enemy-held location, your elite operatives now have orders to identify and eliminate key infrastructure assets, then to escape before the foe’s reinforcements can hunt them down. Unbeknownst to both forces, a lurking apex predator has sensed them as potential prey.

NPOs: This mission is a three-way battle - the player(s) and two opposing sides of NPOs. One NPO side is 1 AMBULL NPO and 2 BOREWYRM INFESTATION NPOs; set them up in reserve (they arrive as per the Intruder deck). The other NPO side, known as the Sentry NPOs, is D6+10 points of NPOs, each set up with a Conceal order wholly within alternating NPO drop zones, starting with a random one.

Player Order: Whenever you would determine initiative, establish an order instead. Roll one D6 separately for the player(s) and each NPO side. The side with the highest result is first, the side with the second highest result is second, and so on. If two or more sides are tied, keep rolling for them until an order is established between them. Activate in the Firefight phase in side order, starting with the side that’s first.

NPO Activation: The AMBULL and BOREWYRM INFESTATION NPOs are activated using the NPO activation deck; draw a card from this deck if any of those NPOs are in the killzone. Activate Sentry NPOs according to the threat principle and they cannot counteract.

NPO Reinforcements: As a Sentry NPO STRATEGIC GAMBIT in each turning point after the first, add D3 points to the NPO Reinforcements pool, then set up NPO reinforcements from that pool. Each reinforcement must be set up ready with a Conceal order with its base touching the NPO killzone edge.
Escape: Player operatives can move over the player killzone edge; if any part of their base does, they’re removed from the killzone and have escaped.
Player operatives can perform the following mission action:

One objective marker the active operative controls is removed from the killzone. Note that whenever an operative finishes performing this action, you must draw a card from the Intruder deck unless it’s empty.
An operative cannot perform this action during the first turning point, or while within control range of an enemy operative.
The battle ends when all player operatives have escaped or been incapacitated. VP is then scored as follows:
For each objective marker that’s been removed from the killzone, the player(s) score 1VP. For each that hasn’t, the NPOs collectively score 1VP.
For each third of the player(s)’ starting operatives that are incapacitated, the NPOs collectively score 1VP.

At the end of the battle, if the player(s) have scored more VP than the NPOs collectively, the player(s) win. If the NPOs collectively have scored more VP than the player(s), the player(s) lose. If the scores are tied, it’s a draw.

Within a ruptured generatorium on the brink of catastrophic overload, two kill teams race to salvage vital power cells and deny them from their foes before the installation becomes irradiated. But time is not the only factor; the imminent meltdown has been caused by a feeding intruder, and it is still here.

NPOs: The AMBULL and two BOREWYRM INFESTATION NPOs are third party operatives set up in reserve (they arrive as per the Intruder deck) and they are activated using the NPO activation deck. After the final player activates, but before the first player activates again, if there’s an NPO in the killzone, draw a card from the AMBULL NPO’s activation deck. In other words, the NPOs activate last in the alternating sequence.

Modified Threat Principle: Whenever an NPO performs an action, the closest visible player operative it could fight/move towards (as determined by the NPO’s behaviour) is its target (or simply the closest if none are visible). If multiple players’ operatives are equally as close to the NPO, roll-off and the winner decides which operative is its target. The opponent of the player who controls that target will control the NPO for that action, and they must make every effort to charge/fight that target (as determined by the NPO’s behaviour) if the NPO can, and move as specified in the Drawn to Energy rule if it cannot.

Drawn to Energy: Whenever an AMBULL or BOREWYRM INFESTATION NPO performs the Reposition or Dash action, move it towards the closest objective marker instead (if possible). Note that it will still perform Fight and Charge actions ahead of those actions as per its behaviour, if able.
Sickening Emissions: Whenever a friendly player operative has an objective marker within its control range, you cannot re-roll their attack or defence dice.
Player operatives can perform the following mission action:
One objective marker the active operative controls is siphoned. Note that whenever an operative finishes performing this action, you must draw a card from the Intruder deck unless it’s empty.

An operative cannot perform this action during the first turning point, while within control range of an enemy operative, or if that objective marker has already been siphoned during this turning point.
At the end of the fourth turning point, the battle ends and the player with the most VP is the winner. If the players are tied, it’s a draw.
Whenever a friendly operative performs the Siphon Power mission action, you score 1VP (to a maximum of 2VP per turning point).
If a friendly operative incapacitates the AMBULL NPO, you score 2VP.

Whenever a BOREWYRM INFESTATION NPO is incapacitated, place a Borewyrm marker underneath the centre of its base. Player operatives can perform the Pick Up Marker action on Borewyrm markers. At the end of the battle, you score 1VP for each Borewyrm marker friendly operatives are carrying.

This mission pack contains rules for the Archivist nemesis operative, alongside two missions designed specifically for it. The first mission is player vs environment (PvE) for co-operative or solo gameplay with the Archivist against NPO adversaries, but the Archivist will betray the players to achieve its own aims. The second mission is player vs player (PvP), but the Archivist acts as a third party operative that players must compete to appease and win to their side. The Archivist can be used in other missions at your discretion.

The ARCHIVIST operative can be a friendly player operative in both missions; note that it doesn’t gain a faction keyword in these instances, so it cannot be selected for your kill team’s faction rules that specify an operative with that faction keyword. When it’s an NPO, use the threat principle and behaviour rules for it as normal. The ARCHIVIST operative is also a NEMESIS operative; it has the Extra Defence and Bulky core NEMESIS rules, but it doesn’t have Towering Size. The ARCHIVIST NPO has the following additional rule:

The ARCHIVIST NPO uses a deck of cards to determine NPO activation. Whenever it’s the ARCHIVIST NPO’s turn to activate, draw a card from the deck and consult the NPO Activation Cards table on each mission to determine how to resolve it. Once you’ve resolved it, discard that card. The ARCHIVIST NPO can be activated twice per turning point. If you draw a card but none of it can be resolved, simply skip that NPO activation. For example, if you draw an NPO activation card and you are instructed to activate a non-ARCHIVIST NPO, but there are no ready non-ARCHIVIST NPOs to activate, discard that card and then the player(s)/next player activates. NPOs cannot counteract in this mission pack, but whenever it’s the NPOs’ turn to activate, still draw a card from the deck (even if all NPOs are expended). This is because the activation card may have other rules effects, such as setting up reinforcements.

The NPO activation deck remains secret and cards are only revealed when drawn. However, players can inspect the discard pile at any time to inform them of activation cards that remain in the deck. In the Ready step of each Strategy phase, and whenever a card would be drawn from the deck but it’s empty, shuffle all NPO activation cards (including discarded ones) together to recreate the deck.
| Range 8", Devastating 3, Piercing 2 | Range 8", Devastating 3, Piercing 2
| Brutal, Shock, Stun | Brutal, Shock, Stun
Core Nemesis Rules: Extra Defence, Bulky.

Behaviour: This NPO will shoot the closest player operative as a priority, but will fight if the need arises and shoot other NPOs. When activated, if it will perform the Fight or Shoot action during that activation, give it an Engage order. Otherwise, give it a Conceal order.
Charge the closest operative with less than 10 wounds remaining.
Reposition towards the closest player operative, to cover if possible (a subsequent Dash action can fulfil this).
Dash towards the closest player operative, to cover if possible.
Xenotech Shielding: Whenever an operative is shooting this NPO:
Normal and Critical Dmg of 4 or more inflicts 1 less damage on this operative.
This NPO can benefit from the effects of the Extra Defence core rule regardless of being injured (this takes precedence over that rule).
Determine the mission between 1: Betrayal (Joint Ops) or 2: Negotiation (Adversary Ops).

If playing mission 1, select a kill team for the player(s) as described in Joint Ops Kill Team Selection. If playing mission 2, each player selects their own kill team. If playing mission 2, roll-off - the winner decides who has initiative. Set up the killzone and objective markers (if any) as specified by the mission map. The mission map for mission 1 uses Killzone: Tomb World, and the mission map for mission 2 uses Killzone: Volkus, but you can use a different killzone and set up terrain features similarly to what’s specified. Set up mission markers (if any) as specified by the mission rules. Drop zones are assigned to the player(s) and NPOs as specified by the mission map. If playing mission 2, the player with initiative selects one drop zone, and their opponent has the other.

The player(s) select their operatives for the battle, adhering to the selection requirements in their kill team’s rules. If playing mission 2, each player does this secretly before revealing their options simultaneously. If playing mission 1, the player(s) select which NPO datacards they’ll be using for the non-ARCHIVIST NPOs. If playing mission 1, the player(s) select up to four equipment options (four in total, not four per player). If playing mission 2, each player secretly selects up to four equipment options before revealing them simultaneously. Each option cannot be selected more than once per player(s)/player. Don’t select equipment for NPOs.
If playing mission 1, the player(s) gain 2CP (two in total, not two per player). If playing mission 2, each player gains 2CP. NPOs don’t gain any CP.

The player(s) set up all their equipment that’s set up before the battle (ladders, etc.). If playing mission 2, each player alternates setting up an item of equipment, starting with the player with initiative (note it’s item by item, not option by option). The mission will specify how many NPOs are set up and where. If playing mission 1, the NPOs are set up before the battle, so set them up now with a Conceal order. If playing mission 2, the ARCHIVIST NPO isn’t set up until later.

The player(s) then set up their operatives. Each operative must be set up wholly within their drop zone and must be given a Conceal order. If playing mission 2, each player alternates setting up one third of their kill team (rounding up), starting with the player with initiative.

If playing mission 1, in the first turning point the player(s) have initiative. If playing mission 2, the players roll-off in the first turning point and the winner decides who has initiative. If it’s a tie, the player who didn’t have initiative during set up decides.

The battle ends when the mission specifies. In mission 2, if one player has no operatives in the killzone but the battle hasn’t ended, the other player plays out each remaining turning point until it does. In both missions, the mission’s victory conditions will specify how to determine the winner.

The Archivist has aligned itself with your elite operatives in a joint venture to seize a cache of artefacts from a fortified vault. Yet, while the alien data trader is a knowledgeable and powerful ally against enemy combatants, experienced warriors will be wary of its fluid loyalties where xenotech is involved.

NPOs: Set up 15 points of NPOs wholly within NPO territory but not within the Vault marked on the mission map. As an NPO STRATEGIC GAMBIT in each turning point after the first, set up D3+2 points of NPOs wholly within NPO territory in the same manner.

Archivist’s Path: Set up the ARCHIVIST wholly within the player drop zone at the point marked ‘A’ at the start of the Archivist’s Path (see mission map). It starts the battle as a friendly player operative. Whenever the ARCHIVIST player operative is activated, it must move along the Archivist’s Path towards the Vault, but all other decisions are made by the player(s). Once the ARCHIVIST becomes an NPO, it follows its behaviour and moves without following the Archivist’s Path.

Xenotech Vault: Operatives cannot be set up within the Vault while the hatchway to the Vault is closed. Player operatives can perform the Pick Up Marker action on the objective marker within the Vault. While a player operative is carrying that marker, it cannot be removed from the killzone and set up again, and it cannot perform the Dash action.
Betrayal: In the Ready step of each Strategy phase after the first, roll one D6, adding the following to the result (these are cumulative):
1 if two or more player operatives are closer to the player killzone edge than the ARCHIVIST player operative is.
1 if it’s the third or fourth turning point.
2 if the objective marker is being carried by a player operative.

On a 7+, or if it’s the fifth turning point, the ARCHIVIST becomes an NPO and follows its behaviour. It’s no longer a player operative for the remainder of the battle. The ARCHIVIST NPO is an enemy operative to all other operatives (and vice versa) meaning other NPOs will try to incapacitate it, and it will try to incapacitate both other NPOs and player operatives.

Threat Principle: Whenever the ARCHIVIST NPO is performing an action in which it moves, moving closer to the objective marker is a high priority (if possible) for the purposes of the threat principle.
Activate the ARCHIVIST NPO. During that activation it has an APL of 2. It cannot activate more than twice per turning point, and it cannot move more than 9" per turning point.
Activate the ARCHIVIST NPO. During that activation it has an APL of 3. It cannot activate more than twice per turning point, and it cannot move more than 9" per turning point.

Draw without replacement. Use New turning point in the Ready step; an empty deck reshuffles before the next draw. Progress is saved for this tab.
The battle ends at the end of the fifth turning point.
At the end of the battle, if a player operative is carrying the objective marker and is in player territory, the player(s) win.
Otherwise, at the end of the battle, if the ARCHIVIST NPO isn’t contesting the objective marker, the player(s) draw.
At the end of the battle, if the ARCHIVIST NPO is contesting the objective marker, or the objective marker isn’t within player territory, the player(s) lose.

Ever the manipulator, the Archivist has leveraged the resources of a kill team to seize infocores from a derelict vessel. Others are hunting the data-rich cores too, however, and the Archivist masterfully plays both sides, seeking to ensure none have the strength to stop it claiming both hauls.

NPOs: The ARCHIVIST NPO is a third party operative. In the Ready step of the second Strategy phase, set up the ARCHIVIST NPO ready with a Conceal order touching the centre of a random neutral killzone edge, or as close as possible. After the final player activates, but before the first player activates again, if the ARCHIVIST NPO is in the killzone, draw a card from the ARCHIVIST NPO’s activation deck. In other words, the ARCHIVIST NPO activates last in the alternating sequence.

Infocore Extraction: Player operatives (excluding ARCHIVIST) can perform the Pick Up Marker action on the Infocore mission markers, and operatives with an APL stat of 3 or more (excluding all changes) can carry two Infocore mission markers at a time. At the end of each turning point, each player gains a number of Negotiation points equal to the number of Infocore mission markers enemy operatives control.

Negotiation: Each time the ARCHIVIST NPO would activate as a result of its NPO activation deck, each player must secretly bid any number of their own Negotiation points (that number can be 0) by putting a number of dice in their hand that corresponds to the number of Negotiation points they want to bid. They then reveal their selections simultaneously. If one player has a higher bid, that player spends the Negotiation points they bid, then controls the ARCHIVIST as a friendly player operative for the duration of that activation. If neither player bid a higher number of Negotiation points, the ARCHIVIST remains an NPO, activates as normal and follows its behaviours.

Modified Threat Principle: Whenever the ARCHIVIST NPO performs an action, the closest player operative within its control range is its target. If no operatives are within its control range, the closest visible player operative controlling an Infocore mission marker it could fight/shoot/move towards (as determined by the NPO’s behaviour) is its target (or simply the closest if none are visible). If multiple operatives that meet the conditions to be the target are equally as close to the ARCHIVIST NPO, roll-off and the winner decides which operative is its target. The opponent of the player who controls that target will control the ARCHIVIST NPO for that action, and they must make every effort to fight/shoot/move towards that target (as determined by the NPO’s behaviour) while doing so. If no player operatives control an Infocore mission marker and no player is controlling the ARCHIVIST, skip the activation and discard that NPO activation card.
